Higher-End Bun Cha in an Intimate Environment
Apr 2025 • Solo
Duong’s is a higher-end restaurant in the Old Quarter serving traditional Vietnamese cuisine. With seating across various levels, Duong’s maintains an intimate environment. 

Turning to the main topic - food. The deep fried spring rolls were fantastic; the filling was well seasoned and differing in texture. The dipping sauce provided a strong but welcome contrast, with the acidity cutting through the richness of the filling. My only thought is that the dish came out far too hot to eat (for a good few minutes).

The signature Bun Cha did not disappoint. The meat was juicy, tender, and full of flavour, as it was partially submerged in the hearty broth. The ‘flatter’ chunks of meat, sandwiched between split shoots, was certainly preferred given the higher level of charring leading to enhanced flavour profile and texture. Perhaps it was for want of not boiling the meat, which is partially submerged and already cooked perfectly, but the broth could have been served a touch warmer.

Staff were welcoming and helpful when required. Though occasionally lacking attentiveness, they dealt seamlessly with a ‘challenging’ table nearby. A final note on ambiance - the combination of a blender in operation and the bassy music downstairs (which I now understand could have been an adjoining property) was unwelcome. My final gripe is that the Whisky Sour was not near sour enough, and rather resembled watered down whisky with overpowering bitters. Otherwise pleasant with the cinammon and smoky twist.

Overall, a very pleasant experience and I would revisit Duong’s when back in Hanoi, and would recommend to friends and colleagues.

Delicious food with inspiring staff (best spring rolls of my life)
Dec 2024 • Solo
I took the cooking class and it was amazing and so worth it. You really get detailed insight into the fresh premium quality ingredients they use in their dishes. I thought one of the spices they used was very special and not something you can commonly get outside of Vietnam and it really changes the flavor profile of the dish. I had the best spring rolls of my life here. I've been to Vietnam almost every year for the past 12 years. Having gone to the cooking class, I know what they put it in and it's really special/different. There were so many yummy ingredients in those spring rolls. Also the amount of care/work that goes into making each dish is impressive. The chicken for their Pho was fresh which means extra care has to be done to prepare it. Their Bun Cha is also quite delicious. I love Bun Cha and have ordered Bun Cha everywhere and I have to say their Bun Cha is not your typical grab and go Bun Cha. It's special. Also I got to meet one of the Chefs there because she taught the cooking class. She's a very talented local female chef who overcame adversity and learned English on her own - she speaks English very well. The people behind the scenes are very inspiring and hard working which makes the food taste all the more sweeter. I think Anthony Bourdain would have been impressed with her grit and the food, and I could totally see him featuring this restaurant in his show if he were still alive. This place is definitely a hidden gem. It's definitely out there in plain sight in the Old Quarter, but the real magic of this place may not be so obvious to everyone.

Super Set Menu
May 2023 • Business
I came at an off hour but food and service were excellent.

My grab taxi could not fit down the street so I had to walk a short distance to reach Doung’s.

It was a nicely decorated three story building. Bar and kitchen were on the first floor and bathrooms were upstairs.

There were a good selection of Vietnamese and Western style dishes. Not sure what to eat I selected the the traditional set menu and that was an excellent choice for the price:

Spring roll two ways - one fried and the other fresh. Fried one was perfectly cooked not greasy while the fresh one had a full shrimp tied on top. 

Beef pho - tender slices of beef, noodles in a delicious soup. 

Grilled Catfish - came with a side of rice noodles and vegetables to wrap and the catfish on a separate grill. The fish sauce was creamy (not like the standard) and added so much more flavor in the roll. One of the best tasting catfish and dishes for this trip.

Black sticky rice - It was a perfect ending to dinner. Sweet rice with cream and vanilla ice cream.

Service was very good throughout the meal. Every dish was explained to me in detail and nicely presented and removed when I was finished.

Decor was thoughtful but roomier and brighter on the upper floors. Cooking classes offered upstairs as well.

Well worth a visit to this restaurant in the old quarter.
